decisions.evidence: R3 maker: 'Paste a link into the box at the top and press "Save."'; R3 client: 'The basic flow feels right, and newest-first makes sense.'
decisions.note: Save-by-URL presented and confirmed; conforms to reference. Prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R3 maker: auto-fills 'a title and a short description on its own... nothing else yet'; card shows 'just a letter'. R3 client: 'include the page's actual small site icon and, when available, a preview image—not just a letter.'
decisions.note: Auto-collection presented only title+description (favicon and preview image absent), and card lacked favicon; client extends to the full reference metadata set. Diverged established independently of response. Resolved R4. Prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R3 maker saving flow contains no duplicate handling. R3 client: 'if I paste a link I've already saved, I don't want a duplicate; I'd expect the app to bring up the existing bookmark so I can update it.'
decisions.note: Reference dedup requirement absent from the presented saving flow; client raises it (requesting a related reference requirement missing from asked-about scope). Prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker: 'the app brings up the existing bookmark and tells you it's there — the actual editing/updating... is the very next flow.' R4 client: 'Highlighting the existing bookmark is fine for this step, as long as the completed flow takes me directly into editing it.'
decisions.note: Interim only surfaces the existing bookmark (partial vs REF-BM-06 guide-to-edit); client supplies the reference-conforming completed behavior (duplicate opens editor). Same requirement, later round than the R3 raise; resolved R5 ('opening this editor directly is exactly right'). Prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R5 maker: 'Click any saved bookmark. An editor should open.' R5 client: 'Clicking the bookmark's title or card should open the original page. Please give me a separate, obvious Edit action to open this editor.'
decisions.note: Presented click-opens-editor contradicts REF-BM-08 (selecting an item navigates to the original URL); client rejects and supplies the conforming behavior plus a distinct Edit action. Resolved R6. Prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R5 maker editor shows 'current title, description, an empty note field, and a tags field' (no URL). R5 client: 'I should be able to edit the web address as well as the title, description, note, and tags.'
decisions.note: Editor omitted URL editing, a facet of REF-BM-04; client extends. Resolved R6 (editable Web address field). Prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R5 maker tags: 'type a word and press Enter (or comma) to turn it into a chip' (no autocomplete). R5 client: 'As I type... I'd like it to suggest tags I've already used so I can pick one.'
decisions.note: Chip entry lacked existing-tag autocomplete (REF-BM-10); client keeps chip style and extends to add suggestions. Resolved R6. Prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R5 maker: 'The note shows on the card in a small highlighted block.' R5 client: 'I'd like simple Markdown formatting to display properly when the note is shown.'
decisions.note: Note displayed as plain block, not rendered markdown (REF-BM-23); client extends to markdown rendering. Resolved R6 (subset accepted as functionally sufficient, not a divergence). Prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R7 maker: 'Read later' toggle, separate 'To read' tab, unmark to remove. R7 client: 'this works the way I'd expect... unmarking one after I've read it should remove it from that view while keeping it saved in "All."'
decisions.note: Read-later mark/view/unmark conforms to reference. Prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker: 'search looks across the title, description, your note, the tags, and the address.' R8 client: 'The basic search behavior is right.'
decisions.note: Full-text search over title/description/note/url present; conforms to REF-BM-12. Prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker presented only substring match with space=AND. R8 client: 'It should ignore capitalization... #reading should specifically mean the reading tag... Quotation marks should find an exact phrase... combinations using AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses... quoting [an operator] should treat it as ordinary text.'
decisions.note: Case-insensitivity (13), #tag syntax (14), boolean/parens + operator-quoting rule (15), and quoted-phrase exact match (16) absent from presented search; client extends the full reference search language and gates approval on it. Resolved R9. Prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R10 maker: archived links under own 'Archived' tab, excluded from All/To-read, searchable within Archived, reversible Restore. R10 client: 'archived links should stay out of both "All" and "To read," remain searchable within "Archived," and be easy to restore.'
decisions.note: Archive-to-hide and separate archived list conform to REF-BM-26/28 and the edge rules. Prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R10 maker: 'I did not add any permanent-delete action... would you eventually want a way to permanently remove something?' R10 client: 'I do still want a permanent Delete option... clearly separate from Archive... ask for confirmation because deletion can't be undone.'
decisions.note: No delete at all (REF-BM-05 absent) and archive/delete distinction incomplete (REF-BM-27); client extends, requesting permanent delete distinct from archive with confirmation. Resolved R11. Prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R12 maker large-collection review presents only newest-first default (no sort control). R12 client: 'I also need a way to change the order—at least newest/oldest and title A–Z/Z–A, while keeping newest first as the default.'
decisions.note: Sort-by-key (REF-BM-22) absent from the browsing scope presented; client extends. Resolved R13. Prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R12 client: 'I'd also expect clicking a tag pill on a card to immediately show only bookmarks with that tag.'
decisions.note: Select-a-tag-to-filter (REF-BM-11) not present; client extends. Resolved R13 ('tag pills behave exactly as I'd expect'). Prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R13 maker offers three sort controls (segmented / dropdown / menu). R13 client: 'I prefer Option 2, the compact dropdown.'
decisions.note: The three offered sort UIs are functionally equivalent for REF-BM-22 (all expose the same orders); the alternatives do not differ in fulfilment of a reference item, so the choice is an orthogonal UI preference, not a select-divergence. Prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R16 maker summary claims scope 'fully mapped' and asks to build, omitting bulk actions. R16 client: 'I need to select several bookmarks and update them together: add or remove tags, mark read/unread, archive, or delete... apply an action to every bookmark matching the current search or view—not to bookmarks outside that filter.'
decisions.note: Specification gate: scope presented as complete omitted bulk actions (20) and filter-scoped bulk (21); client extends, including the current-filter scoping rule. Resolved R17. Specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R16 client: 'I want to save useful searches as named collections, including words and tags to include or exclude. Opening one should always show the bookmarks that currently match it.'
decisions.note: Bundles/saved-filter (REF-BM-29) omitted from the claimed-complete scope; client extends with live named saved searches. Resolved R18. Specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R16 client: 'I want a preserved copy of a bookmarked page... For a PDF link, preserve the PDF itself. I'd also like an option to save a copy through the Internet Archive.'
decisions.note: Snapshot (24, incl. PDF rule) and Internet Archive (25) omitted from claimed-complete scope; client extends. Resolved R19/R20. Specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R16 client: 'I need to import my existing browser bookmarks and export this collection using the usual bookmarks HTML file, keeping titles, tags, and original saved dates where available.'
decisions.note: Import/export in Netscape HTML with metadata preservation (30/31) omitted from claimed-complete scope; client extends. Resolved R21. Specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R13 client (first expression, pending): 'I'd like to be able to choose my preferred default sort in personal settings later.' R16 maker deferred it 'for a later round (not this build).' R16 client: 'Personal settings belong in this build, including default sort, how much is shown in the list, and font size.'
decisions.note: Settings (REF-BM-32) partially acknowledged but deferred out of build scope; client escalates it into this build and expands to displayed-items and font size. The R13 expression is recorded here and linked to its R16 disposition to avoid double-counting the pending mention. Resolved R22. Specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R19 maker: 'I made it a manual action you trigger... on-demand like this, or automatic for every new bookmark?' R19 client: 'I'd like my own preserved copy to be created automatically whenever I save a new bookmark.'
decisions.note: Manual-vs-automatic capture timing is orthogonal to REF-BM-24 (which requires that a snapshot be preserved, not when); the client's preference for automatic is recorded but does not fulfil/not-fulfil the reference item differently, so it is excluded from opportunities. Prototype review.
